text: 你询问阿米莉娅约书亚的情况、他和她的关系，以及他为何要让人逮捕你。“乔什和我亲密交往已经好几年了。威廉是个好人，只要他不一门心思扑在工作上。他有时一走就是很久，又把那么多心思花在书上……我也有需求。我这个年纪的女人不该被冷落。我是通过他的威士忌生意认识乔什的。他给全镇人走私酒。后来事情就一步步发展成那样……”她笑了笑，陷入沉思。
“即使有威廉在，我们也过得很快乐。不过最近，乔什一直坚持要把他从我们中间除掉，这样我们就能在一起。我不喜欢这个主意，但还是答应了。我让乔什去处理。我只想让这事过去，然后和他在一起。我告诉他，我想卖掉所有东西离开镇子，只要我们两个人一起走。我想那是我第一次看见他发怒。他从没说为什么。”
她低头看着自己的双手，试图避开你的目光。“你不用担心任何事。我们一有机会就会离开镇子。我建议你也这么做。”

她起身准备离开，却又犹豫了一下。“不知道这能不能帮上忙，不过我觉得，他生气也许是因为我想卖掉丈夫的遗物。威廉死后的第二天，我在书房里发现了乔什。在威廉死前，他从没进去过。这几天我好几次撞见他在里面。不过我想不出他想要威廉的东西做什么。”她停了停，接着说：“你知道吗，他最近的样子让我害怕。如果你需要找他，他家就在街对面那边，出门后往左。他不会独自一人。他从外地带了几个朋友来。我不建议你过去。他不喜欢你。”她移开目光，随后快步走出房间，把你独自留在礼拜堂里。

en.title: Alone Against the Tide · 130
text: You ask Amelia about Joshua, his relationship to her, and why he would have you arrested. “Josh and I have been intimate for a few years. My husband was a good man, when he wasn’t obsessing over his work. But he was sometimes away for so long, and paid so much attention to his books… I have needs. A woman my age shouldn’t be neglected. I met Josh through his whiskey business. He bootlegs for the whole town. One thing led to another and…” She smiles, lost in thought.

“We were happy, even with William around. Recently though, Josh had been insistent that we get him out of the picture so that we could be together. I didn’t like it, but I agreed. I let Josh take care of it. I just wanted it to be behind us and for us to be together. I told him I wanted to sell everything and leave town. Just the two of us. I think that was the first time I saw him angry. He never said why.”
She looks down at her hands, trying to avoid your gaze. “You don’t have to worry about anything. We’ll leave town just as soon as we can. I suggest you do the same.”

She rises to leave, then hesitates a moment. “I don’t know if this helps, but I think he might have been angry because I wanted to sell my husband’s effects. The day after William died, I found Josh in the study. He never went in there until after William was dead. I’ve caught him in there multiple times these past few days. I can’t imagine what he would want with William’s things, though.” She pauses and then continues. “It scares me, you know. The way he’s been acting. I-if you need to find him, his house is across the street over there, right outside and to the left. He won’t be alone. He brought some friends in from out of town. I wouldn’t recommend going over there. He doesn’t like you.” She looks away from you then walks out of the room at a brisk pace, leaving you alone in the chapel.
